title: U.S. House · Georgia's 6th Congressional District
area: Western suburbs of Atlanta, including parts of Cobb and Fulton counties.

context.text: Incumbent Lucy McBath (D) previously represented the old 6th District (2019-2023) and the old 7th District (2023-2025) before running in and winning this redrawn 6th District seat in 2024; she advanced unopposed from the Democratic primary. Kevin Martin won the Republican primary over Justin Pinker.

candidates.name: Lucy McBath
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 6th Congressional District (since 2025; previously represented Georgia's 7th District 2023-2025 and Georgia's 6th District 2019-2023)

summary.text: Lucy McBath is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 6th Congressional District. A former Delta Air Lines flight attendant, she became a gun-safety advocate after her son was killed in 2012 and was first elected to Congress in 2018, defeating Rep. Karen Handel. She represented the district's earlier boundaries from 2019 to 2023 and Georgia's 7th District from 2023 to 2025, and won the redrawn 6th District in 2024.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Virginia State University in 1982, then interned for former Virginia Gov. Douglas Wilder.
Worked as a flight attendant for Delta Air Lines beginning in the 1990s, relocating to Atlanta, where Delta is headquartered.

After her 17-year-old son Jordan Davis was shot and killed in Florida in 2012, she became a national spokeswoman for Moms Demand Action, joined Mothers of the Movement, and worked as an advocate for Everytown for Gun Safety; she also spoke at the 2016 Democratic National Convention and later authored a book.

Decided in 2018 to challenge Republican Rep. Karen Handel rather than run for the Georgia House; won the Democratic primary runoff over Kevin Abel on July 24, 2018, then defeated Handel in the November 6 general election, 50.5% to 49.5%.

Re-elected in 2020 in a rematch with Handel. After Georgia's 2021 redistricting she ran in the 7th District in 2022, defeating Rep. Carolyn Bourdeaux in the Democratic primary and Republican Mark Gonsalves in the general election.
Won the redrawn 6th District in 2024 against Republican Jeff Criswell with about 74.7% of the vote, and advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 100% of the vote.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), assigned to the House Committee on the Judiciary (Crime and Federal Government Surveillance Subcommittee) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce; earlier terms included Judiciary and Education and Workforce subcommittee assignments. She created a foundation, Champion In The Making Legacy, to help high school graduates continue their education and training.

priorities.text: Says she is fighting to expand access to affordable health care, protect those with pre-existing conditions, and lower the cost of prescription drugs.
With the New Democrat Coalition, released an Affordability Agenda to lower costs in health care, housing, energy, family care, and household essentials.

positions.summary: Serves as Vice Chair of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force and says she was instrumental in passing the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
positions.quote: Since coming to Congress, McBath has been instrumental in passing the Bipartisan Safer Communities Law.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for expanding access to care by fully funding Medicaid and strengthening Medicare's guaranteed benefits.
positions.quote: Expand access to care by fully funding Medicaid and strengthening Medicare’s guaranteed benefits.

positions.summary: Her official site says she believes the country must address climate change while securing a sustainable energy future, and supports increased investment in sustainable energy.
positions.quote: Congresswoman McBath believes we must address climate change while securing a sustainable energy future. She supports increased investment in sustainable energy and increasing incentives for homeowners who utilize solar or other forms of renewable energy.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for increasing the minimum wage.
positions.quote: Increase the minimum wage and ensure workers have a seat at the table.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for rolling back the Trump administration's tariffs.
positions.quote: Restore certainty by rolling back Trump’s tariffs and advancing smarter, durable trade policies.

positions.summary: Her Affordability Agenda calls for cutting red tape and updating permitting and zoning to build more homes.
positions.quote: Cut red tape and update permitting and zoning to build four million homes in the next decade.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Crime and Federal Government Surveillance Subcommittee) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Released the Affordability Agenda with the New Democrat Coalition, a policy roadmap on health care, housing, energy, family care, and household costs.

candidates.name: Kevin Martin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Justin Pinker.

summary.text: Kevin Martin is an accounting and finance professional with more than 35 years of experience, including 25 as a controller, and the Republican nominee for Georgia's 6th Congressional District. He describes himself as a fifth-generation native Atlantan who was born in and lives in Smyrna, and is campaigning on youth education programs, elder care costs, and controlled growth in the district.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he is a fifth-generation native Atlantan, was born in Smyrna, Georgia, and still lives there.
Graduated from Campbell High School; earned a bachelor's degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1989 and a bachelor's degree from Georgia State University in 1998.

Says he has worked in accounting and finance for over 35 years, the last 25 as a controller, across the banking, legal, service, heavy equipment distribution, and building-material and food manufacturing industries.
Describes leadership and mentoring roles with youth, young adults, and employees.
Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the 6th District over Justin Pinker, 70.1% to 29.9%.

priorities.text: Says he will focus on education and youth development programs to attract young families to the district.
Says he wants to address elderly medical costs and reduce what he calls unnecessary tests and drug prescriptions.

Campaign website lists ten issue areas: schools, jobs and the trades, the federal budget, housing, wages, prescription drug costs, community hospitals, crime and policing, the Second Amendment, and defense.

statements.quote: Keep federal law focused on people who have actually done something, no national gun registry, and apply the Constitution consistently across every right it protects.
statements.context: Summary of 'The Second Amendment' on his campaign website's home page

statements.quote: Fund law enforcement properly, fix the federal side of the pretrial release problem, and appoint judges who read the law as written rather than legislate from the bench.
statements.context: Summary of 'Crime and Policing' on his campaign website's home page

statements.quote: A full-time wage should clear the cost of living and keep pace with inflation, without compressing the ladder that makes taking on more responsibility worth it.
statements.context: Summary of 'Wages and Working Families' on his campaign website's home page

statements.quote: Open unused federal land for people to build on, give mortgage terms a real hearing, and keep lending standards honest so we do not repeat the 2000s.
statements.context: Summary of 'Housing' on his campaign website's home page
